description: The 'Public AI' civic coalition expands its campaign to demand democratic oversight of AI in essential services, now supported by pilot transparency portals in three major cities that allow citizens to inspect and contest algorithmic decisions in welfare and housing. The movement successfully pressures two national governments to delay automated decision-making rollouts, framing AI not as a tool of efficiency but as public infrastructure requiring accountability. Its influence grows in local elections, reshaping the political cost of unaccountable deployment.
